Q: Git integration in Visual Studio, are there any macros available? A:

No, visual studio's git integration does not expose the current branch name, tag, repo root, or remote url as built in visual studio macros.

As far as I know, this information is not available through visual studio macros. You can also refer to this issue here: https://github.com/github/VisualStudio/issues/1012

Q: Dompdf stalls when called from Laravel queue worker to convert table with large number of row and pictures to PDF A:

The problem turned out still to be that the job timeout was not set long enough. Once I set public $timeout = 300; on the application server where the job is dispatched, the whole setup started to work properly again.

What I overlooked is that timeout is set when a job is dispatched NOT when the job is executed by a queue worker. My understanding was that when a job is dispatched Laravel only saves minimum information, Job class and parameters to instantiate the job class, into queue driver. Then queue worker will use the minimum information to re-instantiate the job and execute it. My understanding turned out be wrong. Queue worker actually just grabs the job from queue driver and execute it as it is.

The subtle difference is usually not a problem when queue worker runs on the same server as where jobs are dispatched, but becomes one when queue worker runs on a different server and the timeout is tweaked after a job is dispatched. In such cases, whatever timeout is set on the queue worker server won't take effect at all. I learned my lessons, hope my mistake will save someone a bit of time in the future.

Q: Google Cloud Application Default Credentials Permission Denied - Quota Project not set as Default A:

tl;dr.
The error message is wrong, or misleading. You probably need to set the x-goog-user-project header. The documentation for this is right, but is in the wrong place. It would probably be better if the error message just redirected to this stackoverflow thread!

This error message

Your application is authenticating by using local Application Default Credentials. The vision.googleapis.com API requires a quota project, which is not set by default. To learn how to set your quota project, see https://cloud.google.com/docs/authentication/adc-troubleshooting/user-creds ...

...is not true, but also.... not completely unhelpful.

I got a similar error message when using identitytoolkit.googleapis.com , invoking the REST API directly, not through a library. Just using curl etc. And I've also seen this error connecting to sheets.googleapis.com .

I had obtained my token from gcloud auth print-access-token , so the error message "Your application is authenticating by using local Application Default Credentials." was plainly incorrect .

and "The vision.googleapis.com API requires a quota project, which is not set by default." was not quite wrong, but it was not helpful. For me, same as with you, even after setting a quota project for ADC with the suggested step of

gcloud auth application-default set-quota-project [project-id]

..it still gives the same error message. Good for you, for trying the same thing multiple times before surrendering. I did too. But really, we should know that it wouldn't work, because we weren't using ADC to begin with. So, setting the quota project in the ADC way... is bound to not work.

But the error message isn't completely unhelpful, because it's talking about a quota project and billing, independent of ADC. That's a useful hint. Googling around, I found the solution, described here, in the doc explaining how to troubleshoot ADCs

There are two kinds of Google Cloud APIs:

Resource-based APIs, which use the project associated with the resources being accessed for billing and quota.

Client-based APIs, which use the project associated with the account accessing the resources for billing and quota.

When you provide user credentials to authenticate to a client-based API, you must specify the project to use for billing and quota. This project is called the quota project.

There are a number of ways to specify a quota project, including the following options:

  • Update ADC to use a different project as the quota project:
    gcloud auth application-default set-quota-project YOUR_PROJECT

  • If you are calling the REST or RPC API directly, use the x-goog-user-project HTTP header to specify a quota project in each request. For details, see Set the quota project with a REST request.

The part about gcloud auth application-default set-quota-project YOUR_PROJECT is irrelevant for me, because I am not using ADC. But the other part is good info.

Vision, identitytoolkit, sheets, speech... and others I'm sure are (apparently) client-billed APIs, and so if you are going to use the API directly, then you need to use the X-goog-user-project header. eg

curl -s -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
    -H "Authorization: Bearer "$(gcloud auth print-access-token) \
    https://speech.googleapis.com/v1/speech:recognize \
    -H "x-goog-user-project: <project_id>" \
    -d @sync-request.json

WHY, you might ask, is a fact about invoking REST APIs that have special billing requirements, described ONLY in the doc page for troubleshooting ADCs? and I couldn't find this information anywhere else. Diabolical I tell you. It's like telling people to read the documentation on your dishwasher to understand how to start your car.

Notwithstanding the weird location of the information, it is correct, relevant information.

Q: Error retrieving values from ObjectStateEntry A:

My inner exception was The attempted operation is not supported for the type of object referenced

The error would occur when calling SaveChanges on my database context after adding a new entity to the database.

To solve my problem I had to change my entity so that a complex type IPAddress was used instead of a string.

Q: How would I, from a button in html, launch a python file in GitHub? A:

There are a few things wrong on your code.

  1. There's a typo on the src argument. You typed scr, which can't load properly the script.
  2. To my knowledge, a script HTML tag, cannot run Python scripts, just JavaScript and other languages for website development. Maybe you can run python with some backend but also, I don't think pygame can run on a web browser.

If you want to run the script, the proper way should be running "python script.py", I don't get the point of running it on a HTML page.

And the problem of showing the HTML in screen may be that you're not saving that HTML code in a .html or .htm file or you need to use other html tags like html and body for the browser handling correctly that code.

Q: implement jsonp request for python A:

You don't need to, the padding is only needed in browser/JavaScript context to bypass certain security constraints. For Python usage just take the raw response, remove the padding and parse the remaining data accordingly.

from json import loads

a = 'paddingFunction({"a":1,"b":2,"c":3,"d":4,"e":5})'
startidx = a.find('(')
endidx = a.rfind(')')

print(loads(a[startidx + 1:endidx]))
# {'a': 1, 'b': 2, 'c': 3, 'd': 4, 'e': 5}
